statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the adaptation phase (between-factor Age, within-factor Episode)
statistics.quote: We confirmed these observations by analysis of variance (ANOVA) for the adaptation phase, using the between-factor Age and the within-factor Episode: significant effects were yielded for Age (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05), Episode (F(14,308)=41.14, P<0.001), and their interaction (F(14,308)=3.44, P<0.001).
statistics.direction_quote: Most importantly, adaptive improvement was more pronounced for young than for old subjects.
statistics.admissible_reason: Between-participants main effect of Age on pointing error across the 15 adaptation episodes (the perturbation block containing late adaptation).
statistics.notes: Error-like measure (pointing error in deg), so the group with more pronounced adaptive improvement (young) had smaller errors; older subjects therefore higher (a_greater). Exponential fits reported alongside: y=9.92+53.51×exp(−x/5.89) for young and y=29.51+29.91×exp(−x/5.13) for old, but no test statistic attached to the fitted asymptotes.

statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the adaptation phase — Episode effect
statistics.quote: significant effects were yielded for Age (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05), Episode (F(14,308)=41.14, P<0.001), and their interaction (F(14,308)=3.44, P<0.001)
statistics.admissible_reason: Within-participant effect (Episode), not a between-group comparison.

statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the adaptation phase — Age × Episode interaction
statistics.quote: significant effects were yielded for Age (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05), Episode (F(14,308)=41.14, P<0.001), and their interaction (F(14,308)=3.44, P<0.001)
statistics.admissible_reason: Interaction term, not a simple between-group contrast.

statistics.locator: Results, additional ANOVA comparing pointing errors in episodes 20 and 26
statistics.quote: To determine whether the initial reduction of performance differed between age groups, we compared the pointing errors in episodes 20 and 26 by an additional ANOVA; the effects of Age (F(1,22)=13.78, P<0.01) and Episode (F(1,22)=7.79, P<0.05) were significant but not their interaction, in accordance with the view that the initial reduction was not age-dependent.
statistics.direction_quote: Most importantly, adaptive improvement was more pronounced for young than for old subjects.
statistics.admissible_reason: Collapses the last adaptation episode (20) with a refresh-phase episode (26), so it is not a test of late adaptation alone.
statistics.notes: Episode 20 is the final adaptation episode (late adaptation), but episode 26 belongs to the post-break refresh phase; the Age effect here spans both.

statistics.locator: Results, additional ANOVA comparing pointing errors in episodes 20 and 26 — Episode effect
statistics.quote: the effects of Age (F(1,22)=13.78, P<0.01) and Episode (F(1,22)=7.79, P<0.05) were significant but not their interaction
statistics.admissible_reason: Within-participant comparison across episodes, not between groups.

statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the refresh phase (rotation re-instated after break)
statistics.quote: Accordingly, ANOVA yielded significant effects of Age (F(1,22)=13.42, P<0.01) and Episode (F(2,44)=6.18, P<0.01), but no significant interaction.
statistics.admissible_reason: Different phase (refresh phase after the five-minute break), not the end of the initial perturbation block.

statistics.notes: These pages report only F and t statistics with P thresholds, exponential-fit parameters for the adaptation curves (young: y=9.92+53.51×exp(−x/5.89); old: y=29.51+29.91×exp(−x/5.13)), and means±SD for the trail-making test; no Cohen's d, Hedges' g, or eta-squared is given.

parsed.notes: Only the adaptation-phase ANOVA Age main effect (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05) is a between-group test on the pointing-error outcome within the perturbation block; the paper reports no separate contrast for episode 20 alone. Direction is established by 'adaptive improvement was more pronounced for young than for old subjects' — with an error measure this means older subjects (Group A) had larger errors late in adaptation, consistent with the fitted asymptotes (9.92 deg young vs 29.51 deg old). Other statistics on the page (after-effect ANOVA F(4,88)=66.84 and F(4,88)=3.95; tracking transfer ANOVA F(1,43)=144.09; trail-making t(22)=5.25) concern different phases or different measures and were not transcribed as late-adaptation rows.
